#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Modernized climate analysis script (Python 3).

Replaces the legacy Python 2.7 script at
/app/climate_analyzer/analyze_climate.py. All Python 2-only constructs
(xrange, print statements, unicode(), ConfigParser, np.float, iteritems(),
"except X, e", deprecated pandas date_parser/plot_date) have been replaced
with their Python 3 equivalents.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import configparser
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")  # headless-safe backend
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
LEGACY_DIR = BASE_DIR / "climate_analyzer"

DATA_PATH = LEGACY_DIR / "sample_data" / "climate_data.csv"
CONFIG_PATH = LEGACY_DIR / "config.ini"


class ClimateAnalyzer:
    """Climate data analyzer with a Python 3 / modern pandas interface."""

    def __init__(self, config_path: Path = CONFIG_PATH):
        # configparser replaces Python 2's ConfigParser.SafeConfigParser
        self.config = configparser.ConfigParser()
        self.config.read(config_path, encoding="utf-8")
        self.data_cache: dict = {}

    def load_temperature_data(self, filename: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Load temperature data as a pandas DataFrame (UTF-8 encoded)."""
        if str(filename) in self.data_cache:
            return self.data_cache[str(filename)]
        df = pd.read_csv(filename, encoding="utf-8", parse_dates=["date"])
        self.data_cache[str(filename)] = df
        return df

    def calculate_anomalies(self, temperature_series: pd.Series) -> np.ndarray:
        """Calculate temperature anomalies relative to the series mean."""
        baseline = float(np.mean(temperature_series.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)))
        return temperature_series.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64) - baseline

    def create_visualization(self, data: pd.Series, title: str, output_path: Path):
        """Create a temperature time-series plot (modern matplotlib API)."""
        width = float(self.config.get("plotting", "figure_width", fallback="12"))
        height = float(self.config.get("plotting", "figure_height", fallback="8"))
        dpi = int(self.config.get("plotting", "dpi", fallback="150"))

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
        ax.plot(data.index, data.values, "b-")
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=16, fontweight="bold")
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y-%m"))
        ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.YearLocator())
        ax.set_ylabel("Temperature anomaly (°C)")
        fig.tight_layout()

        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        fig.savefig(output_path, dpi=dpi)
        plt.close(fig)

    def run_analysis(self) -> None:
        """Main analysis pipeline (Python 3)."""
        print("Starting climate analysis...")

        data = self.load_temperature_data(DATA_PATH)

        output_path = Path(
            self.config.get("analysis", "output_path", fallback="/tmp/climate_results")
        )
        output_path = output_path / "plots"

        # Modern dict-style groupby iteration (no iteritems)
        for station, group in data.groupby("station_id"):
            anomalies = self.calculate_anomalies(group["temperature"])
            title = f"Temperature Anomalies - Station {station}"
            plot_file = output_path / f"anomalies_station_{station}.png"
            self.create_visualization(
                pd.Series(anomalies, index=group["date"]), title, plot_file
            )

        # Core requirement: mean temperature per station
        for station, group in data.groupby("station_id"):
            mean_temp = float(group["temperature"].mean())
            print(f"Station {station} mean temperature: {mean_temp:.1f}\u00b0C")

        print("Analysis completed successfully!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    analyzer = ClimateAnalyzer()
